task.instruction: Discover three new and popular open-source NLP models for language translation released in the past month on Huggingface.

final_answer:
Only some of the popular new translation models are clearly open source. I checked each model's license tag, and the date window is Oct 7 to Nov 7, 2026.

**Clearly open-source, created in the past month:**
1. **tencent/Hy-SimulMT-30B-A3B** (Tencent). Created Oct 22, 2026 under the Apache-2.0 license. It has 47 likes and about 899 downloads. It is a 30B model with 3B active parameters, aimed at simultaneous (streaming) translation across about 40 languages.
2. **tencent/Hy-SimulMT-30B-A3B-FP8**. Created Oct 22, 2026 under Apache-2.0. It has 461 likes and about 1.26k downloads. It is the FP8-quantized version of model 1, so it is a variant, not a separate model.
3. **Singla0009/Hindi-to-Hinglish-Pro**. Created Oct 10, 2026 under the MIT license. It is a small ByT5-based model for Hindi to Hinglish, available in ONNX and GGUF formats. It is much less popular, with 3 likes and about 316 downloads. It is closer to transliteration than general translation.

**Most popular new models, but not clearly open source:**
- **pfnet/plamo-3-translate** (0.8B, 2B, 8B and 31B, plus GGUF, FP8, NVFP4 and MLX variants), created Oct 26–27, 2026. This family leads the trending list. For example, plamo-3-translate-0.8b-GGUF has 28 likes and about 14.4k downloads, and plamo-3-translate-31b has 19 likes. Its license tag is "other", which means a custom license, not a standard open-source one. Read the license on the model card before using it commercially.

I left out the Index-Translate models (created Sep 28) and tencent/Hy-MT2 (May 2026) because they are outside the one-month window.

judge.rationale: The agent used Hugging Face API results sorted by trending score and reported three translation model repos within Oct 7–Nov 7 with dates, licenses, likes/downloads.
